proof_skeleton_nl: Work directly with the original rational theorem difference Δ_{d,r,n}(q) rather than with an auxiliary parameter or a globally cleared denominator. First extract the arithmetic consequences of n ≡ 1 mod 2d so that Δ_{d,r,n}(q) is well-defined. Next split the target modulus [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 into two independent cyclotomic pieces: the proper-divisor part U_n(q)=∏_{m|n,1<m<n} Φ_m(q), and the primitive nth-root part Φ_n(q)^3. For the proper-divisor part, prove separately that for every proper divisor m of n the rational function Δ_{d,r,n}(q) is locally divisible by Φ_m(q); then combine these local divisibilities into a single divisibility by U_n(q). For the primitive nth-root part, first represent Δ_{d,r,n}(q) with an explicit denominator coprime to Φ_n(q), then prove the bottleneck statement that Δ_{d,r,n}(q) and its first two q-derivatives vanish at every primitive nth root of unity; the abstract multiplicity-three criterion converts that vanishing into local divisibility by Φ_n(q)^3. Finally, combine the U_n(q)-divisibility and the Φ_n(q)^3-divisibility using coprimality and the factorization [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 = U_n(q) Φ_n(q)^3, and unfold the definition of Δ_{d,r,n}(q) to recover the exact theorem statement.

steps.derives: From the theorem hypotheses on d, r, and n, conclude that n is odd, gcd(d,n)=1, the exponent r(1-n)/2 is an integer, and every exponent k(d-dk-2r)/2 occurring in the finite sum is an integer.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the content of Lemma L1 under the theorem hypotheses.

steps.derives: Define Δ(q) = Δ_{d,r,n}(q) = Σ_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k - [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}. Define U(q) = U_n(q) = ∏_{m|n, 1<m<n} Φ_m(q), with the empty product interpreted as 1. Define M(q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.
steps.trivial_justification: This step only introduces abbreviations for the original theorem difference, the proper-divisor cyclotomic product, and the target modulus.

steps.derives: For every divisor m of n with 1 < m < n, there exist polynomials A_m(q) and B_m(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B_m(q), Φ_m(q)) = 1 and Δ(q) = Φ_m(q) A_m(q)/B_m(q).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly Lemma L5 applied to the locally defined rational function Δ(q).

steps.derives: There exist polynomials A_U(q) and B_U(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B_U(q), U(q)) = 1 and Δ(q) = U(q) A_U(q)/B_U(q). Equivalently, Δ(q) ≡ 0 mod U(q).
steps.trivial_justification: Lemma L6 is designed precisely to combine the family of local proper-divisor representations from A2 into one representation with modulus U(q).

steps.derives: Let B_prim(q) = q^{d n(n-1)/2 + r n}(q^{2d};q^{2d})_{n-1}. Then B_prim(q) Δ(q) belongs to Z[q], and gcd(B_prim(q), Φ_n(q)) = 1. Hence Δ(q) can be written as A_prim(q)/B_prim(q) with A_prim(q) in Z[q] and denominator coprime to Φ_n(q).
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly Lemma L2, with A_prim(q) defined to be B_prim(q) Δ(q).

steps.derives: For every primitive nth root of unity ζ, one has Δ(ζ) = 0, (d/dq)Δ evaluated at q=ζ is 0, and (d^2/dq^2)Δ evaluated at q=ζ is 0.
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly the conclusion of Lemma L7 for the rational function Δ(q).

steps.derives: There exist polynomials A_n(q) and B_n(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B_n(q), Φ_n(q)) = 1 and Δ(q) = Φ_n(q)^3 A_n(q)/B_n(q). Equivalently, Δ(q) ≡ 0 mod Φ_n(q)^3.
steps.trivial_justification: Step A4 gives a representation of Δ(q) by a rational function whose denominator is coprime to Φ_n(q). Step A5 supplies the vanishing of Δ, Δ', and Δ'' at every primitive nth root of unity. These are exactly the hypotheses of Lemma L8, so Lemma L8 yields the displayed Φ_n(q)^3-divisibility representation for Δ(q).

steps.derives: One has M(q) = U(q) Φ_n(q)^3 and gcd(U(q), Φ_n(q)^3) = 1 in Z[q].
steps.trivial_justification: This is exactly Lemma L3 after substituting the definitions of U(q) and M(q) from A1.

steps.derives: There exist polynomials A_M(q) and B_M(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B_M(q), M(q)) = 1 and Δ(q) = M(q) A_M(q)/B_M(q). Equivalently, Δ(q) ≡ 0 mod M(q).
steps.trivial_justification: Step A3 gives a localized divisibility representation of Δ(q) by U(q). Step A6 gives a localized divisibility representation of the same Δ(q) by Φ_n(q)^3. Step A7 supplies the coprimality gcd(U(q), Φ_n(q)^3) = 1 and the product identity U(q) Φ_n(q)^3 = M(q). Therefore Lemma L4 applies with A(q)=U(q), B(q)=Φ_n(q)^3, and F(q)=Δ(q), and it yields the required divisibility representation by the full product M(q).

steps.derives: Let [m]_q = (1−q^m)/(1−q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} (1−aq^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.
steps.trivial_justification: Step A8 states that the rational function Δ(q) is congruent to 0 modulo M(q)=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 in the localized rational-function sense. By the definition of Δ(q) from A1, this means exactly that the difference between the finite sum and the right-hand side [rn]_q q^{r(1−n)/2} is congruent to 0 modulo [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2. Rewriting a zero-difference congruence as a congruence between the two sides yields precisely the displayed theorem statement.
